notes:
2026-09-12 (later, live bug report): user saw the Scenarios-tab replay show a single 'Magitek Infantry' chip flip TAPPED after the {2}{W} tutor ability resolved — confusing, since the scenario's own board should have TWO real copies at that point (the original, untouched permanent + the freshly-tutored, genuinely-tapped second copy). Root cause confirmed live + via a direct `replayTrace()` probe: `app/lib/scenarioReplay.ts`'s self-identity tracking (`ensureSelf`, keyed off harness.ts's scenario-domain `instanceId`) and its real-object-identity tracking (`resolveInstance`/`idCards`/`claimedByOtherId`, keyed off `RealCard.id`) are two DISCONNECTED systems — self was never registered into the `id`-keyed one at all, because harness.ts's own `cast`/`activate`/`trigger`/`enters` log entries never carried a real `id` field, only `instanceId`. So the tutored second copy's own `moveTo`+`tap` (real, distinct `id`) has no way to avoid `ensure()`'s `byName` alias, and silently lands on the ALREADY-existing self chip instead of creating a new one — not a rules bug, a replay-renderer identity-merge bug, same CLASS already fixed elsewhere in that file for two same-named FILLER instances (The Crystal's Chosen, fin/14) but never extended to self's own identity. Landed the ENGINE-side half of the real fix (my own domain, harness.ts): `lifecycleBefore`/`lifecycleAfter` (+ the `sequence`-step trigger/activate pushes) now ALSO emit a real `id: selfReal.id` on every self-identifying entry (`cast`/`activate`/`trigger`/`enters`/`playLand`/`move`), additive, alongside the pre-existing `instanceId` — confirmed in this card's own regenerated trace.json: `activate` now carries `id:6` (self) vs the tutored copy's own `moveTo`/`tap` `id:3` (genuinely different real objects). Documented in `.claude/contracts/state-event-format.md`. This is INERT on its own (243 functional-model + 22 scenarioReplay.test.ts tests unchanged, verify-synergy clean) until `app/lib/scenarioReplay.ts` (card agent's own file, out of engine's lane) is updated to register self's own `id` into `idCards`/`claimedByOtherId` inside `ensureSelf`, so a later `moveTo`/`tap` carrying a genuinely different `id` creates a separate chip instead of aliasing — confirmed live (screenshot) the merge bug is STILL visibly present pending that consumer-side fix. Scenario itself was NOT trimmed to drop the tutor ability despite this — its own `result:` text is already fully honest about what happens (a real second copy enters tapped; the static +1/+0 is text-only, no CDA hook) and this project's own standing convention is to fix/document a real bug a scenario surfaces, not curate the board to avoid exposing it; the tutor ability is also this card's OTHER real distinct mechanic, worth its own coverage independent of the CDA-limited pump, and this exact merge-bug class will recur on any other 'find another copy of yourself' card regardless of whether this one scenario keeps demonstrating it.

2026-09-12 (later): added `excludeSelf: true` to the condition sink (`to:'Battlefield', types:{has:['Artifact']}, amount:{min:1}`) — the real oracle text is 'as long as you control ANOTHER artifact,' and the Facts tab notes column was rendering the fact with no trace of that qualifier at all (same class of bug flagged live on G'raha Tia's own 'another creature or artifact' dies sink). New `Constraints.excludeSelf` field (functional-model/synergy.ts), display-only via app/lib/factConditions.ts — does NOT change matching: this card's own earlier note already established `amount` (and now `excludeSelf`) are never consulted by `factsInteract`, so a real second copy of this card still correctly self-matches as `selfInteractionKind:'second-copy'`, unaffected by this addition. `review` reset from 'human' back to 'ai' — this is an authored-content change to `synergy.json` per project convention (a stale 'reviewed' flag must never survive a content change), so this card needs a fresh human pass.

2026-09-12: trimmed to 1 scenario (real success path only), per user's explicit effort-calibration correction ("1 scenario is enough... not testing engine edge cases") — dropped the 'no second copy found'/'empty library' no-op scenarios, folded the static artifact-threshold premise into the same real-success scenario's own setup. verify-synergy/vitest clean.

Migrated to the unified Fact model (was old string-key/id/sourceText v1-ish shape, 1 bare sink fact). 6 facts, all annotated: self-cast/self-enters baseline, event:'pump' for the +1/+0 threshold (same real engine gap as Gaelicat's own 'control two or more artifacts' — no threshold-CDA machinery, see isMagitekInfantryArtifactThresholdPumpFact), a real Constraints-based condition sink for 'another artifact' (to:'Battlefield', types:has:['Artifact'], amount:{min:1} — amount is never actually matched by factsInteract, confirmed, so no self-exclusion mechanism was needed; a real second copy of this card correctly self-matches as selfInteractionKind:'second-copy'), and a genuine NAME-specific tutor pair (SOURCE from:'Library' to:'Battlefield' name:{eq:'Magitek Infantry'} tapped:true, value:1; SINK to:'Library' name:{eq:'Magitek Infantry'} value:-1 for the precondition). Added pt:[1,1] to definition.ts (was missing entirely). Added harness.ts PlayerState.libraryNamedCount/libraryNamedCard (first name-addressable library seed field) and a new scenario demonstrating the tutor's real success path (moveTo+tap trace evidence) — previously structurally impossible with the old harness.
knownGaps: the +1/+0 threshold CDA and its own condition-sink amount:{min:1} are both real, honest DATA with zero possible trace/read evidence — this engine has no threshold-CDA machinery at all (same documented gap as Gaelicat); both exempted via narrowly-scoped verify-synergy.mjs functions, not silently tolerated

the tutor SOURCE fact's own subject:'self' happens to also satisfy isActivationCostPermanentBaselineFact's over-broad predicate (any subject:'self'/target:'self' zone fact on an activationCost permanent) — not a false pass here (real scenario evidence exists regardless) but flagged as a latent, unfixed exemption looseness worth tightening pool-wide someday

Scenarios-tab replay renderer bug (app/lib/scenarioReplay.ts, card agent's own file, not this card's own data): the tutored second copy's moveTo+tap visibly merges onto the ALREADY-on-battlefield original Magitek Infantry chip instead of appearing as its own separate, correctly-tapped chip — engine-side groundwork landed (harness.ts's self-identifying log entries now carry a real `id`, see .claude/contracts/state-event-format.md), consumer-side fix (register self's `id` into scenarioReplay.ts's own idCards/claimedByOtherId set) still open, needs card agent
oracleTextSnapshot:
This creature gets +1/+0 as long as you control another artifact.
{2}{W}: Search your library for a card named Magitek Infantry, put it onto the battlefield tapped, then shuffle.
